title: Nerd Research DAG
description: Schema for the nerd research knowledge graph. Per-project files store theories, verdicts, build infrastructure profiles (build_profile, cache_verdict), rubric instruments (rubric, triangle_verdict), and edges. The global index stores synthesis nodes and tool_availability nodes. Infra nodes use I-prefixed IDs; rubric nodes use R-prefixed IDs; triangle-verdict (judge-calibration) nodes use TRI-prefixed IDs. Most node types use status active|stale; rubric_node uses active|deprecated (deprecated = superseded by a forked rubric_id), so a generic consumer enumerating aged-out nodes by status:stale should also account for deprecated rubric nodes.

theory_node.description: A competing hypothesis about why a system behaves a certain way.

source_experiment.description: Experiment ID that generated this theory, e.g. E001

source_files.description: File paths this theory is about

codebase_hash.description: 8-char SHA hash of sorted source file contents at time of creation

status.description: Active = current, stale = source files changed since creation

tags.description: Category tags for matching and synthesis clustering

spawned_from.description: Verdict ID that spawned this theory, if any

research_type.description: Distinguishes research types. 'parameter' = tunable-value sweep; 'performance' = perf benchmark (theories go stale faster — codebase_hash should be scoped to profiled functions, not whole codebase); 'experiment' = any other falsifiable experiment with a numeric metric (model/prompt comparison, ablation) fitting neither category; 'hypothesis' = a single-commit / single-change sweep-of-one test (the /nerd-this brief mode). Optional — nodes may omit it.

verdict_node.description: The outcome of testing a theory via experiment.

theory_id.description: ID of the theory this verdict evaluates

source_experiment.description: Experiment ID that produced this verdict

rubric_id.description: Optional — present only for rubric-judged experiments (instrument_kind: judge_rubric). Library id of the rubric this verdict was judged against, e.g. 'portrait-v3'.

rubric_hash.description: Optional — sha256 (64 hex) of the rubric YAML at judging time. Pins the verdict to exact rubric content.

judge_id.description: Optional — the judge model used, e.g. 'claude-opus-4-7'.

triangle_verdict_id.description: Optional — the triangle_verdict node that admitted this judge instrument.

criterion_scores.description: Optional — per-criterion scores from the rubric. Keys are criterion names; values are numeric scores (e.g. Likert means) or booleans (e.g. pass/fail flags like face_drift).

allOf.$comment: Rubric-judged verdicts must carry full provenance. If rubric_id is present, the rest of the rubric fields become required — this catches a partially-written rubric verdict at validation time. Numeric verdicts (no rubric_id) are unaffected.

build_profile_node.description: Build infrastructure profile for a project — dependency count, build times, artifact sizes. Created by lab-tech Check 7. Language-agnostic.

source_files.description: Files that affect build profile, e.g. Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock

cache_verdict_node.description: Success/failure record for a build cache strategy. Written by report-compiler after experiment batches.

strategy.description: The cache strategy that was tested (e.g., sccache, ccache, artifact_copy, incremental, none)

runs_tested.description: Number of batch runs this verdict covers

failure_count.description: Number of CACHE_FALLBACK events if FAILED

tool_availability_node.description: Record of a build cache tool detected on this machine. Global scope (project: null in the global index).

path.description: Absolute path to the tool binary

synthesis_node.description: A pattern observed across 3+ verdicts, potentially cross-project. Stored in index.json.

supporting_verdicts.description: Qualified references to verdicts supporting this synthesis

rubric_node.description: A reference to a pre-registered rubric used as a judging instrument. The authoritative rubric content lives in the YAML library file (.nerd/rubrics/<id>.yaml); this node references it by content hash so any criteria change forces a new hash (and, per strict pre-registration, a fork to a new rubric_id). Written by report-compiler.

rubric_library_id.description: Library id — the YAML file basename without extension, e.g. 'portrait-v3'

version.description: Informational version metadata from the rubric YAML. Not a migration mechanism — substantive change forks to a new rubric_id.

content_hash.description: sha256 (64 hex) of the canonicalized rubric YAML. The cryptographic pin for strict pre-registration.

source_path.description: Repo-relative path to the rubric YAML, e.g. .nerd/rubrics/portrait-v3.yaml

created_by.description: Optional — author of the rubric at first registration.

status.description: active = current; deprecated = superseded by a forked rubric_id

triangle_verdict_node.description: A cached judge-instrument calibration verdict: whether a given judge can discriminate a rubric's stimuli in a blind triangle test. Cached per (rubric_hash, judge_id) and reused within the rubric's freshness window. Structural twin of cache_verdict_node — result carries the PASS/FAIL outcome, status carries the active/stale lifecycle. Written by report-compiler from lab-tech's readiness report.

id.description: Triangle verdict node ID, e.g. TRI001

rubric_hash.description: sha256 (64 hex) of the rubric YAML at verdict time — pins the verdict to specific rubric content.

correct_count.description: Trials where the judge correctly identified the odd-one-out. Must be <= total_trials (enforced as a runtime assertion by report-compiler before writing — JSON Schema cross-field comparison is not used in this schema).

result.description: PASS = judge discriminates the rubric's stimuli above chance (binomial p<0.05); FAIL = cannot discriminate.

verified_at.description: When this calibration was run. Freshness is computed against the rubric's triangle_cache_days at read time.

edge.description: A relationship between two nodes with explanatory context.

description: A DAG file — either a per-project file or the global index.

edges.description: Relationships between nodes. Present in project files, optional in index.

project_path.description: Absolute path to project root, for collision detection
